us2_founding.topic: Founding documents and structure: US Constitution (Article V, Tenth Amendment, federalism) vs Israel's Basic Laws (count, entrenchment, Torah Study 2026), unitary local government

claims.text: US Constitution Article V: amendments proposed by two-thirds of both Houses (or a convention called on application of two-thirds of state legislatures) and ratified by three-fourths of the states; 27 amendments, the last in 1992
Tenth Amendment (1791): 'The powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution, nor prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States respectively, or to the people.'

Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation s.7: 'shall not be varied except by a Basic Law passed by a majority of the members of the Knesset'; s.8 override: a law violating it has effect if passed by a majority of MKs, expressly states so, and expires after four years

Basic Laws list: The Knesset 1958 (s.4 electoral system amendable only by 61 MKs), Israel Lands 1960, President 1964, Government 1968/1992/2001, State Economy 1975, Military 1976, Jerusalem 1980, Judiciary 1984, State Comptroller 1988, Human Dignity and Liberty 1992 (32-21), Freedom of Occupation 1994, Referendum 2014, Nation-State 2018, Torah Study 2026; Bank Mizrahi (1995) held laws violating limitation clauses void

Basic Law: Torah Study passed 13 July 2026 by 63-52; declares Torah study a 'foundational value'; Movement for Quality Government petitioned the High Court immediately, calling the package 'a draft exemption law through the back door'; Likud's Edelstein and Illouz voted against; Netanyahu absent

Israel is a unitary country with one level of subnational government: 258 local authorities in 2021 (76 municipalities, 126 local councils, 56 regional councils); subnational spending 12.8% of public expenditure and 5.9% of GDP (2020); grants 54.0% and taxes 39.7% of subnational revenue; council bylaws and budgets subject to Interior Ministry approval
OECD: Israeli local governments are funded mainly by central-government grants and the arnona property tax, levied by physical size rather than value
OECD review of Israeli local government finance makes 13 recommendations, including a longer-term move from the floor-area arnona to a value-based property tax

us2_courts.topic: Courts and the 2023 overhaul in Israel; US Supreme Court checks on the executive (IEEPA tariffs); trust in courts over time; prosecutions of leaders

claims.text: Basic Law: The Judiciary (Amendment No. 3), adopted 24 July 2023, barred all courts from assessing the reasonableness of decisions of the government, PM or ministers, including appointments; reasonableness review was a judge-made standard for 'extremely unreasonable' decisions

1 January 2024: High Court struck down the reasonableness amendment 8-7, the first time a Basic Law was annulled; per ToI 13 of 15 justices held the court may review Basic Laws (Wikipedia gives 12); Hayut: the law 'does the most severe harm possible to the principle of the separation of powers'; Mintz dissent: 'something out of nothing'; amendment had passed 64-0

27 March 2025: Knesset passed Judicial Selection Law in second and third readings after 71,023 opposition objections and an opposition boycott; drops the two Bar Association members, adds a coalition-chosen and an opposition-chosen lawyer, gives coalition and opposition vetoes over Supreme Court appointments; takes effect in the next Knesset

14 December 2025: a seven-justice High Court panel, unanimously, annulled the August 2025 cabinet dismissal of Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara because the changed dismissal procedure (Resolution 3125) was adopted without factual or legal basis; she remains in office; Levin called the ruling 'unlawful intervention'; Karhi urged the government to dismiss her anyway

20 February 2026, Learning Resources v. Trump (with Trump v. V.O.S. Selections): Supreme Court held 6-3 (Roberts) that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs ('IEEPA contains no reference to tariffs or duties'); CBP identified about $166bn collected from over 330,000 importers; Section 122 replacement tariffs from 24 February 2026

Gallup Sept 2026: 61% disapprove of the Supreme Court (tied record), 34% approve; 54% have not very much or no trust in the judicial branch; trust first fell below 50% in Sept 2022, never before in Gallup's trend since 1972

IDI Democracy Index 2025 (22 Dec 2025): for almost all institutions trust is below the multi-year average; among Arab respondents the Supreme Court is the most trusted institution, 'albeit only at 41%'

Netanyahu, charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust (denies), trial since 2020, the first sitting PM charged; asked President Herzog for a pardon in November 2025; on 26 April 2026 Herzog said efforts should first be exhausted to reach an agreement; Trump repeatedly urged a pardon

Ynet: AG and state attorney agreed 4 May 2026 to plea talks; prosecutors finished cross-examining Netanyahu after 94 court days (16 June 2026); he completed testimony after 98 hearings (24 June 2026); 29 June 2026 headline on why judges want the bribery charge dropped

Ehud Olmert began a 19-month prison term in February 2016 for bribery (about $130,000, Jerusalem housing project while mayor), the first former Israeli PM imprisoned; former president Moshe Katsav was serving seven years for rape

us2_emergency.topic: Emergency powers: Israel's declared state of emergency since 1948 and its legal dependants; US National Emergencies Act declarations over time

claims.text: The Supreme Court on 8 May 2012 rejected ACRI's 1999 petition to end the state of emergency in force since 1948, saying the petition 'has exhausted itself, although the work has not been finished'; Basic Law: The Government (1992) limits each declaration to one year with unlimited renewals; every government has renewed it; some contentious emergency laws remain

The emergency was authorised by s.9 of the Law and Administration Ordinance adopted 19 May 1948; it now rests on s.38 of Basic Law: The Government (2001); the Knesset has renewed it every time; 204 emergency regulations on labour and economic matters were issued 1974–1982; in 2012 the court issued a decree nisi requiring progress updates before dismissing the petition

Adalah (2003): s.9 emergency regulations, the Prevention of Terrorism Ordinance 1948 and the Prevention of Infiltration Law 1954 depend on the declared emergency; the Defence (Emergency) Regulations 1945 'remain in force' and 'are not dependent on an officially declared state of emergency'; Israel's 3 October 1991 ICCPR notice says the 1948 emergency 'has remained in force ever since' and derogates from Article 9
Brennan Center: 51 declared national emergencies in effect as of 19 October 2026

Brennan Center (17 May 2022): 75 national emergencies declared in 44 years under the NEA, 41 still in effect; 68 of 75 primarily to impose IEEPA sanctions; the oldest in effect is Carter's 1979 Iran hostage-crisis emergency

Cato (14 Sept 2026): 52 active emergencies per the Brennan Center's September 2026 tally; Trump's second-term declarations include a January 2025 national energy emergency and IEEPA tariff emergencies on synthetic opioids, migration and trade deficits; the Supreme Court held IEEPA does not authorise tariffs

us2_integrity.topic: Civil service and corruption measures: Transparency International CPI 2012–2025 for both; US federal workforce cuts 2025 and Schedule Policy/Career; IDI on Israel's CPI decline

claims.text: US CPI 2024: 65, 28th of 180, four points below 2023, the lowest since the 2012 scale; peak 76 in 2015
US CPI 2025: 64, 29th of 182, lowest ever; TI cited 'actions targeting independent voices and undermining judicial independence' and the FCPA enforcement freeze

IDI (18 Feb 2026): Israel CPI 2025 62, 35th of 182, down from 64 and 30th; about 74% of Israelis surveyed think corruption more widespread than in the past; cites challenges to the independence of police, the AG's legal advisory system and the judiciary, and expanded political appointments in government companies

OPM final rule on Schedule Policy/Career published February 2026: policy-influencing career positions moved into the excepted service without standard removal procedures; bars patronage and use for mass layoffs; positions placed by executive order

GovExec 5 Feb 2026: rule effective 8 March; officials estimated up to 50,000 employees could be covered; AFGE promised a court challenge; Stier: can be used 'to remove expert career federal employees'
Reuters 5 March 2026: federal civilian workforce shrank 12% between September 2024 and January 2026; Treasury -24%, HHS -20%, DHS +<1%

OPM director Kupor (Dec 2025): about 317,000 federal employees left in 2025, incl. ~144,000 deferred resignations, ~24,000 involuntary separations (17,000 RIFs, 7,000 probationary), ~21,000 early retirements/buyouts, ~129,000 routine attrition; ~68,000 hired by end of August
Axios: US has not been in the top 20 'cleanest' countries since 2017
